> Thanks, Ben. Sarah, I've attached our proposed DPA redlines (redlines_v3.docx). Key points to note from the legal side:
>
> - Transfers: Redwood relies on EU SCCs (2021 version) for EEA exports and maintains a UK addendum for UK transfers. If HealthCore requires a different transfer mechanism we can discuss but SCCs are our standard.
> - Subprocessors: we provide a current register and will notify HealthCore 30 days prior to adding a subprocessor; we can discuss any high-risk subprocessors for exception handling.
> - Audit rights: Redwood's standard approach is to provide SOC 2 Type II reports and penetration test summaries under NDA. We do not typically grant unrestricted customer-led audits of our facilities or supplier networks. For customers with specific regulatory needs, we can negotiate a scoped, remote audit limited to controls relevant to the customer's data and only after exhaustion of available attestation reports.
> - Scope & indemnities: we proposed a few language tweaks around breach notification timelines and data deletion timelines in the redlines.
>
> Please review the attached redlines and let us know whether HealthCore will accept attestation evidence in lieu of a full on-site audit. If you need a tailored audit clause, provide the acceptable scope and frequency (e.g., remote, one per 12 months, 30 days notice) and we will take that back to security for feasibility.
